title: GLM-4.5 ARC: Agentic, Reasoning, and Coding Foundation Models
content: GLM-4.5 is an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts large language model from Zhipu AI (Z.ai), published as arXiv:2508.06471, with 355B total parameters and 32B active parameters per forward pass; a compact variant, GLM-4.5-Air, uses 106B total and 12B active. The model was trained on 23 trillion tokens and post-trained through multi-stage reinforcement learning with expert model iteration, producing a hybrid reasoning architecture that switches between an explicit thinking mode and a direct-response mode. The ARC framing — Agentic, Reasoning, Coding — names three co-designed capability pillars: deep tool integration and agent-framework compatibility, interleaved chain-of-thought reasoning, and software-engineering task performance. On standardised benchmarks GLM-4.5 scores 63.2 across 12 industry benchmarks (ranked third overall, second on agentic tasks), 91.0 on AIME 2024, 64.2 on SWE-bench Verified, and 70.1 on TAU-Bench. Full BF16 inference requires 16 H100 GPUs; FP8 quantisation halves that requirement; models are released under MIT licence on Hugging Face and ModelScope.
lesson: GLM-4.5 establishes the ARC capability triad — Agentic, Reasoning, Coding — as the architectural contract for autonomous systems engineering, demonstrating that a 32B-active-parameter MoE can match much larger dense models on tool-use and SWE benchmarks; this maps directly to ark's operator layer, which must select, test, repair, and audit strategies through multi-step agentic loops rather than single-shot inference.
key_usages: drive the agentic strategy-engineering loop (state → action → feedback → revision)
tool-calling over the evidence court to fetch backtest results and regime signals
interleaved chain-of-thought reasoning when auditing strategy logic for leakage or overfitting
coding subtasks: generate, patch, and test operator pipeline components
switch to non-thinking mode for low-latency regime classification at execution time

key_codes.label: serve GLM-4.5-Air via vLLM (FP8, tool-call parser enabled)
key_codes.code:
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --served-model-name glm-4.5-air

key_codes.label: serve GLM-4.5-Air via SGLang (FP8, speculative decoding)
key_codes.code:
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

key_codes.label: (illustrative) OpenAI-compatible tool-call from ark operator loop
key_codes.code:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url='http://localhost:8000/v1', api_key='x')
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='glm-4.5-air',
    messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': state_prompt}],
    tools=ark_tools,
    extra_body={'chat_template_kwargs': {'enable_thinking': True}}
)
